question: The radius of a right circular cylinder is thrice of its height. If the height of the cylinder is 2.1 cm, then what is the volume of cylinder?
solution:
Given:

The radius of a right circular cylinder is thrice of its height. 

Height of the cylinder is 2.1 cm.

Concept used:

Volume of a cylinder = πR²H

where r = Radius of the base, h = height

Calculation:

Radius = 3 × 2.1 = 6.3 cm

The volume of the cylinder

⇒ π × 6.3² × 2.1

⇒ 261.954 cm3 ≈ 261.95 cm3

**∴ The volume of the cylinder is 261.95 cm3.**
